title: Bill would let federal whistleblowers sue if disciplined over violating NDAs
summary: New legislation from Virginia Democrats seeks to beef up federal whistleblower protections as the Trump administration weighs drastically expanding agencies’ use of non-disclosure agreements.

title: What 9/11 can teach federal families about benefits
summary: The federal workers’ compensation program can provide critical support after a work-related injury, illness or death, but families need to know what to document and which benefits to claim.

title: USPS workers most impacted by mail-in ballot EO haven’t been trained yet, union warns
summary: If the Supreme Court clears the way for USPS to implement the Trump administration’s mail-in ballot executive order, the American Postal Workers Union says its members will have little time to prepare for these changes.

title: Don’t let federal agencies judge their own discrimination cases
summary: COMMENTARY | The current system would leave workers at the mercy of the agencies they accuse of discrimination, argues AFGE's civil rights leader.

title: Trump signs veterans benefits order calling for improved data sharing
summary: The order instructs the departments of Veterans Affairs and Defense to conduct a broad review of information technology-related contracts to ensure greater interoperability.

title: GSA announces per diem increases for feds this fall
summary: Beginning in October, the amount federal agencies reimburse employees for daily lodging associated with official travel will increase by at least $3.

title: Trump is staffing up agencies with political appointees. They’re not sticking around, new analysis finds
summary: The Partnership for Public Service previously reported on high turnover among Senate-confirmed political appointees during the president’s second term. In a new report, researchers from the nonprofit find a similar trend with non-Senate-confirmed ones.

title: For federal executives, retirement means losing more than a job
summary: COMMENTARY | Retirement planning often focuses on benefits and finances. For senior federal employees, leaving government can also mean giving up a title, mission and professional identity, while agencies face the loss of decades of expertise.

title: Air traffic controllers are still waiting on 2.8% of their congressionally approved pay raise
summary: Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford says the agency needs to improve how it uses its existing workforce before he will release the rest of the increase.

title: CDC, after months of delays, gives employees 20 days to resubmit disability accommodation documentation
summary: CDC is spending months, if not longer, to process reasonable accommodation requests because HHS-wide layoffs and separation incentives decimated the department’s human resources functions.

title: NSA looks to AI to help analysts sift through vast data troves
summary: The tools can speed up work that takes days or weeks, the agency’s cybersecurity chief said.

title: Musk should testify about overstated savings from DHS contract cancellations, Democrats argue
summary: The Government Accountability Office reported that contract terminations pushed by the Department of Government Efficiency yielded a net of $92 million — much less than the Homeland Security Department’s public report of as much as $10.5 billion in potential savings.

title: FEMA’s future looks clearer. Disaster aid is still uncertain
summary: The emergency management agency is rebuilding after a year of upheaval, but the Trump administration’s approach to disaster declarations and federal recovery funds is leaving states unsure what support they can count on.

title: USDA employees dispute ‘inflated’ claim that most staff asked to relocate will do so
summary: USDA employees say they have nothing to lose by saying they plan to relocate, even if they have no intention of moving, or are only considering it as a last resort.

title: Former pardon atty calls MSPB ‘a dead end,’ sues for reinstatement
summary: Liz Oyer, who was fired from her position as pardon attorney last year over her refusal to recommend that Mel Gibson’s right to own a firearm be restored, said the Justice Department did not follow its own policies when it removed her.

title: Reliable rules for your retirement recordkeeping
summary: Pro-tip: Don’t let messy files stall your federal exit.

title: Former CISA employee pleads guilty to defrauding government with secret contractor jobs
summary: Prosecutors say Richeline Fung secretly held contractor jobs tied to six agencies and claimed up to 33-hour workdays while working full time for the federal cyber agency.

title: Inspectors general are facing an identity crisis. Here’s how some former IGs would preserve the watchdogs’ independence
summary: A panel of former leaders of the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency made several recommendations for reforming the group, which has been targeted by the Trump administration.

title: OPM taps new healthcare and insurance chief ahead of Open Season
summary: Matthew Kiley will take over as the division prepares for Open Season following a round of workforce cuts.

title: The National Science Foundation is building out the government’s AI research infrastructure
summary: A new center will help the agency expand access to the computing power and other resources researchers need to develop artificial intelligence.

title: Scammers are making the government harder to trust
summary: COMMENTARY | As government impersonation scams proliferate, agencies face a growing challenge: convincing Americans that legitimate calls, texts and other messages are actually from the government.

title: Inspector general fired by Trump talks leadership, OIG independence and his new memoir
summary: Former Labor watchdog Larry Turner writes about confronting racism, working under “toxic” bosses and what he misses most about being in government.

title: TSP funds were back in the black in August
summary: After two months of stock market slowdowns, the federal government’s 401(k)-style retirement savings program saw each of its offerings increase in value again.
